Saved data is not validated after parsing.
Prices and descriptions are hardcoded and may go stale.

terms.meaning: a small permanent storage space in a web browser, kept for one website
a secret code that lets a program use a paid AI service under an account
the company that runs an AI model and offers it through an interface
the value used when the user has not chosen anything

sections.name: ModelProvider
sections.title: Provider names
sections.what: Names the three AI companies the app can use: together, anthropic, and openai.
sections.why: Limits the provider choice to known values, so a typo is caught before the app runs.
sections.watch_out: Adding a provider here also requires a matching entry in the options list below.

sections.name: ModelSettings
sections.title: Saved settings shape
sections.what: Defines the saved choice: a provider, a model name, and an optional API key.
sections.why: Keeps the user's model choice in one consistent shape.
sections.watch_out: The API key is optional and is saved together with the other settings, which makes it readable from browser storage.

sections.name: MODEL_OPTIONS, DEFAULT
sections.title: Model options and default
sections.what: Lists the three selectable models with names, prices, descriptions, and whether each needs a key. Sets the default to a model through Together that needs no key.
sections.why: Drives the model picker, and the default means a new user can start without entering a key.
sections.watch_out: The price text is typed by hand and will go stale, and the default model name must match an option exactly.

sections.name: getModelSettings
sections.title: Reading the saved choice
sections.what: Reads the saved model choice from browser storage, or returns the default when nothing is saved or the data is broken.
sections.why: Likely reason: falls back safely so the app still works if storage is empty or unreadable.
sections.watch_out: The parsed data is returned without checks, so a well-formed but wrong saved value will be used as is.

sections.name: saveModelSettings
sections.title: Saving a choice
sections.what: Writes the model choice to browser storage.
sections.why: Pairs with the reading step so the choice survives page reloads.
sections.watch_out: It does nothing on the server, and the saved key is readable by any script running on the same page.

summary: Holds the list of AI models the app offers and remembers the user's chosen model in the browser.
purpose: Lets the user pick a provider and model, and saves that choice between visits.
why: Browser local storage keeps the choice on the user's device without needing an account. Likely reason: no server storage is needed for a simple preference.
how: 1) List the available models with their names, prices, descriptions, and whether they need an API key. 2) Set a default model that needs no key. 3) On the browser, read the saved choice or fall back to the default. 4) Write a new choice when the user changes it.
inputs: The user's model choice and optional API key from the settings screen.
outputs: A settings object with a provider, a model name, and an API key when one was entered.
risks: API keys are saved in plain text in local storage, which any script running on the same page can read. Saved data is not checked after it is read. Prices are typed text and may become wrong.
debug: If the wrong model is used, clear the saved settings entry in browser local storage (the key name is set in the file) and reload. If a key is rejected, check the provider key page linked in the options. If the default appears when a choice was saved, the saved data may not parse.
